in which i get to drawing topics i HATE - starting with busy ceilings

yeah, ceilings are the worst

though what I've learned when drawing any environment it is often best to focus on filling the space via tones, rather than trying to draw out what is happening in the background if you are trying to illustrate

because the background should not overwhelm your foreground, even if there is a lot of detail put into it

too much detail you will lose your subject easily, and in the end as far as aesthetic choice goes if your focus is on the subject a busy background does you no favors

edit: another thing that helps is always shade in the way you think a shadow will cast, regardless of the actual tone or aesthetic you are going for (simple vs. realistic)

it is a pain but it will keep areas from having weird out of place perspective or flat textures

the hardest thing to actually do with regards to proficient art is understanding light. It isn't easy, but once you do your drawings change substantially. The day I understood how to manipulate light in my work, was the day I realized how I had been drawing wrong my entire life
